newsitem.title: UK: Funds cut dlr exposure Feb-to-May - Merrill survey.
newsitem.headline: Funds cut dlr exposure Feb-to-May - Merrill survey.

text.p: Fund managers reporting overweight currency exposure in dollars fell sharply to 54 percent in May from a record high 74 percent in February, according to Merrill Lynch's quarterly global investor survey.

In a commentary on the survey, Merrill's head of research Michael Rosenberg said that while investors unwound a substantial part of long dollar positions during the period there remains a preference to be net short of marks and yen.
"Now that those excessive overweight dollar readings have been erased, the dollar appears in a better position to make new headway," said Rosenberg.

The quarterly survey, which polled 93 large international investors around the world, showed Merrill's net weighted average index of dollar exposure fell to 61.50 in May from 71.50 in February - the highest level since the survey began in 1989.
A reading at 50 would indicate a net neutral positioning.

Elsewhere, the Merrill survey showed investors' net positioning in yen rose from a low at 27 in February to 37.75 last month. The equivalent positioning for marks, guilders and Swiss francs rose to 45.50 from 39.50.
Net exposure to sterling slipped to 52.50 from 58.50.
